notes.pest_disease: Slugs and aphids are common lettuce pests. Bottom rot caused by Botrytis can develop in cool, wet conditions. Ensure good air circulation and avoid overhead irrigation.
notes.harvest_marker: Cut-and-come-again at 3-4 inches for baby leaf. Full heads harvested when compact and dense, before bolting begins. Morning harvest preferred for crispness.
notes.storage_handling: Store at 0-2 degrees C with high humidity. Wash and spin dry gently before storage. Use within 7-10 days. Avoid ethylene-producing fruits nearby.
notes.rotation_companion: Rotate with brassicas or alliums. Companion planting with chives or basil may reduce aphid pressure.
notes.cultivar_recommendation: Butterhead varieties like Buttercrunch perform well in warm conditions. Batavian types such as Nevada are heat-tolerant. For baby leaf mix, use looseleaf varieties.
notes.growing_tip: Direct seed or transplant depending on season. Keep soil temperature below 25 degrees C for good germination. Shade cloth in summer extends the season.
notes.irrigation: Regular, consistent moisture prevents tip burn. Drip irrigation at the base reduces disease pressure.
notes.nursery_specific: Germinate at 18-20 degrees C. Transplant at 3-4 true leaves. Harden off seedlings for 5-7 days before field planting.
